QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_1

question.text: Lotus Growth AIF, a close-ended Category II fund, drew down INR 50 crore from investors on 01-Jan-2019 as a single capital call. On 31-Dec-2023, the fund distributed INR 115 crore to investors as its terminal distribution (no interim distributions). Ignoring fund-level fees, what is the approximate Gross IRR of Lotus Growth AIF over its 5-year life?

explanation.text: The Logic: Gross IRR solves: 50 = 115 / (1+IRR)^5, i.e., (1+IRR)^5 = 115/50 = 2.30. Taking the 5th root: 1+IRR = 2.30^(1/5) = 1.1813, so IRR ≈ 18.13%. This is the classic single-outflow-single-inflow IRR shortcut. The Trap: 15% is a rough arithmetic eyeballing; 23% incorrectly annualizes (115-50)/50 / 5 and inflates; 13% is closer to the Net IRR once fees/taxes eat the gross return (the PDF example returns Net IRR ≈ 12.98%).
